## Proof

**Claim.** Yes. The double adjoint $\phi^{**}:A^{**}\to B^{**}$ maps positive operators to positive operators. In fact $\phi^{**}$ is a normal completely positive map between the enveloping von Neumann algebras.

We prove positivity; complete positivity then follows by applying the same argument to each amplification $\phi^{(n)}:M_n(A)\to M_n(B)$.

### 1. Setup and identifications

Let $\pi_u^A:A\to\mathcal B(H_u^A)$ and $\pi_u^B:B\to\mathcal B(H_u^B)$ be the universal representations. The enveloping von Neumann algebras are
$$A^{**}\cong \pi_u^A(A)'' ,\qquad B^{**}\cong \pi_u^B(B)''.$$
Under these identifications the canonical embeddings $\iota_A:A\hookrightarrow A^{**}$, $\iota_B:B\hookrightarrow B^{**}$ correspond to $\pi_u^A$ and $\pi_u^B$, and the weak$^*$ topology $\sigma(A^{**},A^*)$ coincides with the $\sigma$-weak (ultraweak) topology on $\pi_u^A(A)''$, likewise for $B$.

The bitranspose $\phi^{**}:A^{**}\to B^{**}$ is, by construction, $\sigma(A^{**},A^*)$-to-$\sigma(B^{**},B^*)$ continuous; i.e. **$\phi^{**}$ is normal**. Moreover $\phi^{**}\circ\iota_A=\iota_B\circ\phi$, so $\phi^{**}$ extends $\phi$.

### 2. Density of the positive cone (Kaplansky)

By the Kaplansky density theorem applied to $\pi_u^A(A)\subseteq\pi_u^A(A)''$, the unit ball of $\pi_u^A(A)_+$ is *strongly* dense in the unit ball of $\pi_u^A(A)''_+$. On bounded sets, strong convergence implies $\sigma$-weak convergence. Hence

$$\iota_A(A_+)\ \text{is }\sigma\text{-weakly dense in }A^{**}_+.$$

Equivalently: every $x\in A^{**}_+$ is the $\sigma$-weak (weak$^*$) limit of a **bounded** net $(a_\alpha)\subset A_+$.

### 3. Positivity of $\phi^{**}$

Let $x\in A^{**}_+$. By Step 2, choose a bounded net $(a_\alpha)\subset A_+$ with $a_\alpha\to x$ weak$^*$ in $A^{**}$.

Since $\phi$ is completely positive, it is in particular positive, so $\phi(a_\alpha)\in B_+\subseteq B^{**}_+$.

By normality (weak$^*$-continuity) of $\phi^{**}$,
$$\phi^{**}(x)=\phi^{**}\!\bigl(\text{w}^*\text{-}\lim a_\alpha\bigr)=\text{w}^*\text{-}\lim \phi^{**}(a_\alpha)=\text{w}^*\text{-}\lim \iota_B(\phi(a_\alpha)).$$

The positive cone $B^{**}_+$ of the von Neumann algebra $B^{**}$ is $\sigma$-weakly closed (it is the set $\{y\in B^{**}_{\mathrm{sa}}:y\geq 0\}$, cut out by the $\sigma$-weakly continuous functionals $\omega\mapsto\langle y\,\xi,\xi\rangle$). Therefore the weak$^*$ limit of the net $\iota_B(\phi(a_\alpha))\in B^{**}_+$ again lies in $B^{**}_+$:
$$\phi^{**}(x)\in B^{**}_+.$$

Since $x\in A^{**}_+$ was arbitrary, $\phi^{**}$ maps positive operators to positive operators. $\quad\blacksquare$

### 4. Complete positivity (remark)

For each $n\ge 1$, the amplification $\phi^{(n)}:M_n(A)\to M_n(B)$ is positive (because $\phi$ is completely positive). $M_n(A)^{**}\cong M_n(A^{**})$ and $M_n(B)^{**}\cong M_n(B^{**})$ as von Neumann algebras, and $(\phi^{(n)})^{**}=(\phi^{**})^{(n)}$. Applying the result of Step 3 to $\phi^{(n)}$ gives $(\phi^{**})^{(n)}$ positive for every $n$, i.e. $\phi^{**}$ is completely positive. Together with normality from Step 1, $\phi^{**}$ is a **normal completely positive** extension of $\phi$.

### Conclusion

$\phi^{**}:A^{**}\to B^{**}$ does map positive operators to positive operators; indeed it is the canonical normal completely positive extension of the ccp map $\phi$ to the enveloping von Neumann algebras.

### PROOF COMPLETE
